description:
## Why
Elixir raises `UndefinedFunctionError` with `message: nil` and builds the text in `UndefinedFunctionError.message/1`, so `e.message` is `nil` and `Exception.message(e)` is the text. fz fills the field: `runtime/src/failure.rs` `raise_undefined_function` formats the three wordings ("is undefined or private", "is undefined", "is undefined (module X is not available)") in Rust and stores them in `message`. A program that reads `e.message` prints the text on fz and an empty line on Elixir. Fixture 00869 met this and reads `Exception.message(e)` instead.

The wording also lives twice: `lib/exceptions/undefined_function_error.fz` `undefined/4` already builds it when `message` is nil.

## What changes
`raise_undefined_function` raises with `message: nil`; the text comes from `UndefinedFunctionError.message/1` alone, and the Rust formatting of the atom case is deleted. The uncaught banner already renders through `Exception.message` (fz-3sy.9).

## Signal
A fixture with `# oracle: self` prints `e.message` of each miss (nil on all three) next to `Exception.message(e)`, and its golden matches Elixir. 00869 still passes. Check whether the banner and rescue paths still print the same text on run, interp and build.
title: A call that finds no function raises UndefinedFunctionError with message nil, as Elixir does
